body:
### Motivation
- CI runs that restore a cached `.venv` can break when the hosted Python toolcache is rolled forward and venv entrypoints (shebangs) point to a non-existent interpreter, causing errors like `.../.venv/bin/pip: cannot execute: required file not found`.
- Manual installs typically create a fresh `.venv` so they do not see this failure, therefore the installer should detect and recover from stale cached venvs in CI.

### Description
- Add a `venv_is_runnable()` helper to `install.sh` that verifies `.venv/bin/python` and `.venv/bin/pip` are executable by running `.venv/bin/python -c 'import sys; print(sys.executable)'` and `.venv/bin/pip --version`.
- If the check fails, the script removes and recreates `.venv` with `python3 -m venv .venv` and sets `NEW_VENV=true` so the rest of the install path treats it as a fresh environment.
- This change is limited to the venv validation/recreation step and preserves the existing activation, pip bootstrap, and requirements-install flow.

### Testing
- Ran a syntax check with `bash -n install.sh`, which completed successfully.
- Executed `./install.sh --no-start`, which completed the dependency installation and database migrations successfully (no `pip` entrypoint failure observed).

## Summary

- **Navbar.jsx**: Removed duplicate `handleLogout` and `useEffect` declarations that were introduced when PR #56 (edit-profile) was merged alongside PRs #53/#54 (tournament-create-auth, logout-button). Unified into a single `useEffect` that checks auth state and closes the mobile menu on route change, and a single `handleLogout` that clears all auth-related localStorage keys (`authToken`, `loggedIn`, `userId`, and wizard data).

- **LoginPage.jsx**: Changed `localStorage.setItem("token", ...)` to `localStorage.setItem("authToken", ...)` so the stored JWT key matches what `CreateTournament*.tsx`, `TournamentsPage.tsx`, and `Navbar.jsx` all read.

- **ProfilePage.jsx**: Changed both `localStorage.getItem("token")` calls to `localStorage.getItem("authToken")` for consistency.

## Root Cause
PR #56 was based on a branch that used `token` and `loggedIn` as localStorage keys, while PRs #53/#54 (merged into main first) introduced `authToken`. The GitHub merge combined both code paths, creating duplicate declarations (build error) and key mismatches (auth not working across pages).

## Test Plan
- [x] `npm run build` passes cleanly (was failing with duplicate symbol error before)
- [x] Login via `/api/auth/login` returns JWT and stores as `authToken`
- [x] Profile page reads `authToken` and fetches user data successfully
- [x] Logout clears all auth keys
- [x] CreateTournament pages correctly read `authToken`

body:
Buyers/Sellers need a self-service way to delete accounts while retaining anonymized transactional history and blocking deletion when disputes/orders are active.

- **Deletion service**: New `UserAccountDeletionService` enforces blocking rules (active orders/open return cases), strips credentials/external tokens, anonymizes user profile, saved addresses, order payloads, reviews/questions/ratings, login audits, and logs a `UserAdminAudit`.
- **UI flow**: Privacy settings page adds a confirmed “Delete account” form that calls the service, signs out the user, and explains impact/retention.
- **Wiring**: Service registered in DI; deletion endpoint uses `SignInManager` and passes actor info for audit.
- **Tests**: Added coverage for blocking conditions and end-to-end anonymization across related records.

Example (service use & anonymization):

```csharp
var result = await _deletionService.DeleteAsync(user.Id, user.Id, "User self-service", ct);
// Orders now carry scrubbed names/emails; user credentials removed; audit recorded.
```

> ## User Story
> As a Buyer or Seller I want to delete my account with proper anonymization so that my personal data is removed while necessary transactional history is preserved for legal reasons.
> 
> ## Acceptance Criteria
> - Given I am logged in and have no blocking conditions (e.g. open disputes), when I request account deletion, then the system informs me about the impact (loss of access, data anonymization).
> - Given my account deletion is confirmed, when the process completes, then my login credentials and personal identifiers are removed or irreversibly pseudonymized, and I can no longer sign in.
> - Given past orders and financial records must be retained, when anonymization runs, then personal attributes (name, email, phone, address) in those records are replaced with anonymized values while business-critical fields (amounts, dates, product ids) are kept.
> - Given an account deletion occurred, when an admin checks the audit log, then they can see who triggered the deletion, for which account, and when, without exposing the deleted personal data.
> 
> ## Notes
> - Align retention rules with legal and tax requirements in target markets.
> - Design anonymization routines per entity to avoid partial leaks.

body:
## Summary
This PR enhances the coupon system with usage limit tracking and improves the admin coupon management interface with full internationalization support. It adds server-side coupon validation during order creation and implements plan-gated access to the coupon feature.

## Key Changes

### Coupon Usage Tracking
- Added `maxUsage` and `usageCount` fields to the Coupon model to track and limit coupon redemptions
- Implemented server-side coupon validation in order creation that checks:
  - Coupon expiration status
  - Usage limits (if maxUsage is set)
  - Minimum order requirements
- Automatically increments `usageCount` when a valid coupon is applied to an order
- Coupon validation endpoint now rejects coupons that have reached their usage limit

### Admin UI Improvements
- Fully internationalized the coupon management interface (English and Traditional Chinese)
- Enhanced coupons table to display:
  - Usage count with visual indicators (red text when used up)
  - Status badges showing "Expired", "Used up", or "Active/Inactive"
  - New "Usage" column showing current/max usage
- Added delete confirmation dialog with localized messaging
- Improved coupon modal form with:
  - Max Usage field (optional, leave blank for unlimited)
  - Better form validation with localized error messages
  - Reorganized layout with expires date in its own row

### Plan Gating
- Added feature flag check for coupon functionality requiring "lite+" plan
- New `/api/features/coupon` endpoint to check if coupon feature is enabled for a tenant
- Checkout page conditionally displays coupon input based on feature availability

### Order Processing
- Server-side coupon code parsing and validation (prevents client-side discount manipulation)
- Coupon code is now included in order amounts for audit trail
- Discount calculation respects coupon type (percentage vs fixed amount)
- Special handling for "FREESHIP" coupon code to cap discount at delivery fee

### Translations
- Added 30+ new translation keys for coupon management UI
- Covers all form labels, validation messages, status indicators, and action buttons
- Supports both English and Traditional Chinese

### Motivation
- Ensure finished-match recaps always show correct per-goal info including stoppage formatting (e.g. `45+4`, `90+11`), penalty/OG markers `(Pen.)`/`(OG)`, and prevent duplicate or “Unknown scorer” lines. 
- Fix cases where goal metadata (added time, penalty, OG) exists in richer FotMob sections but was ignored because the code picked the first non-empty source.

### Description
- Collect goal candidates from all prioritized FotMob sections in order: `content.events`, `content.matchFacts.events`, `content.matchFacts.events.events`, `content.incidents`, then `content.shotmap.shots`, instead of stopping at the first non-empty source.

## Summary
- Fixes #112: "Failed to write config file" error when ZeroClaw starts

## Root Cause
The `config_path` and `workspace_dir` fields are computed paths (derived from `$HOME/.zeroclaw`) that were being serialized to the config file. When loading from TOML:
1. If these fields weren't in the file, they'd deserialize as empty paths
2. If they were in the file with stale values, `save()` would write to the wrong location
3. Either way, calling `save()` would fail

## Changes
- Add `#[serde(skip)]` to `config_path` and `workspace_dir` fields
- Set computed paths in `load_or_init()` after deserializing from TOML
- Ensures paths are always correct regardless of config file contents

body:
## Context

In large multi-project workspaces, all discovered projects activate simultaneously via `Promise.all`, creating a CPU spike that can saturate all cores during startup. This is part 2 of 3 targeted improvements to language server performance at scale (Part of #1625).

## Summary

Limits the number of projects that activate and validate concurrently during `syncProjects` to prevent CPU spikes when many projects are discovered.

- Replaces `Promise.all` with a generic `runWithConcurrencyLimit<T>` worker-pool pattern (default concurrency limit: 3)
- All projects still activate and validate, but CPU load is spread over time
- Configurable via `ProjectManager.projectConcurrencyLimit`
- Moves `void this.validate()` out of `Project.activate()` into a separate concurrency-limited phase in `syncProjects` (Phase 1: activate, Phase 2: validate — fire-and-forget so interactive features aren't blocked)
- Adds `syncGeneration` counter to cancel stale activation/validation when a new sync arrives
- Adds `cancelValidate()` to `Project.dispose()` to stop in-flight validation on teardown

## Test plan

- [x] New tests verify concurrent activations do not exceed the configured limit
- [x] New tests verify all projects eventually activate and validate
- [x] New tests verify generation counter cancels stale work on re-sync
- [x] New test verifies `dispose()` cancels in-flight validation
- [x] Existing `syncProjects` tests pass unchanged

Replaces the single event processing loop in `NexusWatcher::start` with 3 parallel tokio tasks, each with its own interval and shutdown handling:

### Motivation
- Make the companion minimap convey threat importance more clearly via tiered glyphs and pulsing cues so players can prioritize targets quickly.
- Reduce visual clutter at high enemy density with a density-aware scaling and optional aggregation so the map stays readable on mobile.
- Improve feedback for ability impacts with propagating rings and a short directional tracer from the chopper for clearer situational awareness.
- Add colorblind-safe palette and a high-contrast mode to meet accessibility needs while keeping rendering cheap to preserve a 60fps feel.
- Mirror the companion cues in the in-game HUD for consistent cross-device UX.

### Description
- Companion client drawing: added threat tiers (`BOSS`, `ELITE`, `NEAR_FORT`, `NORMAL`) with distinct glyphs and tiered pulse sizes, and logic to pick tier from enemy metadata. Changes live in `companion/client/app.js` (threat glyphs, pulse/sizing logic).
- Dynamic decluttering: implemented density-aware icon scaling and optional grid-based aggregation clustering; clusters render a count badge; buckets reused across frames to avoid allocations (`declutterBins`, `minimapTmp`).
- Impact rendering: multi-ring propagation on impact and a short directional tracer from the helicopter origin to the impact point (impact messages capture `from` when chopper data exists); cached tracer gradient used to minimize allocations.
- Accessibility toggles: added `colorblind-safe` palette and `high-contrast` mode, persisted to `localStorage`, and injected two small toggle buttons next to existing controls; body classes (`cb-safe`, `high-contrast`) drive CSS variants in `companion/client/style.css`.
- Performance/allocations: switched to a single cached canvas context (`minimapCtx`), reuse of a scratch point (`minimapTmp`), cached gradients and cluster buckets to keep the draw path allocation-light.
- HUD mirroring: updated `karen_defense/ui/hud.gd` to mirror threat-tier visuals (tiered dot sizes, pulsing rings) and added a compact legend for boss/elite/near-fort counts so in-game HUD matches companion cues.
- Styling: added small styles for the toggles and high-contrast/colorblind body variants in `companion/client/style.css`.

### Testing
- Ran `node --check companion/client/app.js` to validate the client script syntax and it succeeded.
- Attempted an automated browser render + screenshot to validate visual behavior (Playwright/Chromium), but Chromium crashed with SIGSEGV in this environment so a screenshot could not be produced; logic and rendering code remain unit/linelike-checked by the `node --check` run.
- No runtime errors were observed during static checks; visual QA is recommended on a device/emulator to confirm pulses, clustering thresholds, and accessibility toggles visually.

author: parameshn
body:
This PR adds `@InheritableMustCall("close")` annotations to the **JDBC** interfaces `Statement `and `ResultSet`.

These types represent database-backed resources whose lifecycle already requires callers to invoke `close().` Adding **MustCall** annotations enables the **MustCall** Checker to detect resource leaks in common **JDBC** usage patterns while refining the existing **AutoCloseable** contract.

This PR contributes to https://github.com/typetools/checker-framework/issues/6354
 by annotating additional **JDK** subtypes of **AutoCloseable** that own external resources.

Related tests are provided in https://github.com/typetools/checker-framework/pull/7480
.

This PR intentionally includes only **JDBC** types. **Audio/MIDI** annotations from the original PR are being handled separately because their lifecycle semantics are more complex.
